profile.reading:
This building's dual codename, TRP3 and SAT46, points toward Microsoft's Texas Research Park cluster of sites in the far west San Antonio area, the same general area where trade press has reported a separate Microsoft building called SAT40 at 15000 Lambda Drive in Bexar County, built on a 70 acre parcel of a larger 158 acre tract Microsoft purchased there in 2015 for roughly $175.9 million. OSM's own location tag for this building places it in Medina County rather than Bexar County, and this building's coordinates sit about 4.3 miles from the tightly clustered trio of buildings this registry tracks separately as Microsoft SAT80, SAT81, and SAT82 on Potranco Road near Castroville, a gap large enough, combined with the county line difference, that this registry treats TRP3 as a physically separate Microsoft site from that Potranco Road campus rather than a fourth building sharing its campus facts. This research could not independently confirm through primary sourcing whether TRP3 sits on the identical parcel as SAT40 or on a separate nearby Texas Research Park area parcel that simply shares Microsoft's regional naming convention, so no campus level acreage, building count, or square footage figure is asserted here for TRP3 specifically.

Microsoft has built at least eight data centers across the San Antonio region, spanning Bexar and Medina counties, since first opening two facilities there in 2015 at roughly $90 million each, with cumulative investment exceeding $1.2 billion as of August 2023. Other named Microsoft addresses reported in the region include 3545 Wiseman Boulevard and 5150 Rogers Road, alongside the separately tracked SAT14 building on Wiseman Boulevard, which trade press has described as 411,000 square feet built across four planned phases through 2024. San Antonio's city council approved a 15 year Chapter 380 tax reimbursement in 2013 covering 40 percent of property taxes in exchange for a $250 million Microsoft investment commitment and the creation of 20 high paying jobs, building on an earlier 10 year property tax abatement the city had approved in 2007 for Microsoft's original San Antonio project. Construction phases at Microsoft's San Antonio area campuses have typically employed several hundred workers, while each completed data center building tends to run with a comparatively small operating staff once online.

CPS Energy, San Antonio's municipally owned electric and gas utility and the largest such public utility in the country, supplies power to Microsoft's San Antonio area sites and has cited large commercial and industrial customers, data centers among them, in its own integrated resource planning as it weighs new generation to meet growing demand. Because CPS Energy is municipally owned rather than investor owned, large load agreements with customers like Microsoft are negotiated directly with the city owned utility rather than through the Public Utility Commission of Texas process that governs most of the state's investor owned utilities. No address, square footage, or megawatt figure specific to this individual building was found in sourcing reviewed this session.

The TRP3/SAT46 to Texas Research Park/SAT40 connection is inferential (shared naming convention and rough area) and explicitly flagged as unconfirmed rather than asserted as fact. reading.body:
Microsoft TRP3, a data center in Medina County near San Antonio, carries dual facility codes suggesting it belongs to Microsoft's Texas Research Park cluster in far west Bexar and Medina counties. This building sits about 4.3 miles from Microsoft's tightly clustered SAT80, SAT81, and SAT82 campuses near Castroville and is treated as a separate physical site, though the exact building footprint and power capacity are not published. Whether TRP3 occupies the same parcel as the previously reported SAT40 facility at 15000 Lambda Drive, built on a 70-acre tract Microsoft purchased in 2015, remains unconfirmed by Microsoft.

Microsoft has invested over 1.2 billion dollars across at least eight data centers in the San Antonio region since 2015, and TRP3 is one of them, operating under a 15-year property tax reimbursement approved by San Antonio city council in 2013. No individual megawatt figure, square footage, or certification status for this building has been published. Texas as a whole has 133 mapped data center facilities with only 19 publishing power figures, totaling 475 MW of disclosed capacity, so most facilities in the state remain opaque to public capacity accounting.

CPS Energy, San Antonio's municipally owned utility and the country's largest public electric utility, directly negotiates load agreements with Microsoft rather than through the Public Utility Commission of Texas. Whether TRP3 represents incremental demand on CPS Energy or consolidation of demand already counted against earlier Microsoft commitments in the region is not disclosed in published specifications.
